structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, in a time-calibrated molecular phylogeny the Perissodactyla share a more recent common ancestor with Lagomorpha (Leporidae) than with Artiodactyla/Cetartiodactyla (other ungulates), and Leporidae share a more recent common ancestor with Perissodactyla than with Rodentia.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Both conditions hold, using TimeTree median divergence times for species pairs: (A) the Perissodactyla-Leporidae divergence time (Equus caballus, Ceratotherium simum, Tapirus terrestris vs Oryctolagus cuniculus, Lepus spp.) is more than 5 Myr younger than the Perissodactyla-Cetartiodactyla divergence time (same perissodactyls vs Bos taurus, Sus scrofa, Camelus dromedarius); and (B) the same Perissodactyla-Leporidae time is more than 5 Myr younger than the Leporidae-Rodentia time (Oryctolagus/Lepus vs Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus, Cavia porcellus). Equivalently, the topology places Perissodactyla+Leporidae as a clade that excludes Artiodactyla and Rodentia.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if either (A) or (B) fails: the Perissodactyla-Cetartiodactyla divergence time is equal to or younger than Perissodactyla-Leporidae (within 5 Myr), or the Leporidae-Rodentia divergence time is equal to or younger than Leporidae-Perissodactyla (within 5 Myr). Current phylogenetics places perissodactyls in Laurasiatheria (with Cetartiodactyla and Carnivora) and lagomorphs with rodents in Glires (Euarchontoglires). Under that tree Perissodactyla-Leporidae is the older divergence (about 90 Myr or more), which would refute the claim.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'more closely related' is read as recency of common ancestry (sister-group or clade membership), not overall similarity. His evidence was a skull transformation, a geometric grid deformation, which is not itself evidence of ancestry. 'Other Ungulates' is mapped to Cetartiodactyla (artiodactyls plus cetaceans). 'Leporidae' is mapped to rabbits and hares, and 'rest of Rodentia' to Rodentia, whose sister group is Lagomorpha in Glires. Modern reinterpretation: the measurable quantity is molecular divergence time in a time-calibrated phylogeny.

dataset.name: TimeTree (Timetree of Life)
dataset.why_it_fits: TimeTree reports median and confidence-interval divergence times between any two taxa, compiled from published molecular phylogenies. Pairwise queries (Perissodactyla vs Lagomorpha, Perissodactyla vs Cetartiodactyla, Lagomorpha vs Rodentia) give the times that decide conditions A and B. Fields used: taxon A, taxon B, median divergence time (Myr), confidence interval, and number of studies as a robustness check.
